artifacts.synopsis: The SJC dismissed the complaint as judicially out of order because it targeted actions of a congregational meeting rather than any act or decision of a court of the Church, as required by BCO 43-1. A dissenting opinion by RE Jack Wilson and seven others argued that the Complainants had sufficiently identified an act of the Session (calling the congregational meeting with the stated purposes) to present a justiciable issue.

artifacts.synopsis: The SJC reported that South Florida Presbytery responded to the citation issued by the 43rd General Assembly. The SJC found most responses satisfactory, but found one response unsatisfactory (regarding charges against a TE that were not properly processed under BCO 32-2), and noted an additional exception of substance regarding improper divestiture under BCO 46-8.

artifacts.title: Thompson v. South Florida Presbytery
artifacts.synopsis: The SJC sustained Thompson's complaint, finding that the Granada Session's judicial commission procedurally erred in imposing excommunication for contumacy before trial because Thompson's behavior did not constitute the immediately censurable kind of contumacy under BCO 32-6.b, and that failing to reach a BCO 38-1 agreement should have led to a trial rather than a pre-trial judgment; the SJC annulled the excommunication and restored the matter to its pre-judgment status as of June 26, 2015.

artifacts.title: Session of First Presbyterian Augusta v. Savannah River Presbytery

matches.evidence: 2004-07 — Session of 1st Presbyterian Church, Augusta, GA v. Savannah River Presbytery Court: Standing Judicial Commission · Assembly: 33rd (2005) · Disposition: sustained · Dissent: yes Source

BCO 25-2 does not give members of the congregation an unfettered right to require the session to call a congregational meeting to conduct business of the congregation's choosing. The session, under our Constitution, retains the responsibility to determine whet

artifacts.synopsis: The Standing Judicial Commission sustained the complaint of the Session of First Presbyterian Church, Augusta, finding that Savannah River Presbytery erred in annulling the Session's actions to dissolve the official relationship with eleven ruling elders. The SJC held that BCO 25-2 does not prohibit a Session from adding agenda items to congregational meetings called pursuant to petitions, and that BCO 24-6 does not prevent a Session from informing the congregation of this right and recommending its exercise.

artifacts.title: Steve Newton vs. Heartland Presbytery & Grace RPC Session vs. Heartland Presbytery
artifacts.synopsis: The Session of Grace Reformed Presbyterian Church appealed its conviction for contumacy and termination of its relationship with Heartland Presbytery. The SJC reversed the conviction, holding that a presbytery lacks original jurisdiction to indict and try a session (lower court) for an offense such as contumacy, as BCO provisions reserve original jurisdiction over ruling elders to the Session level.
